full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This Rule on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the proceeding in GR case No. 305 of 2007 arising out of Badda PS case No. 98 dated 25-4-2007 under sections 143/447/427/506 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No.15, Dhaka should not be quashed. 

 3. On the basis of FIR, Badda PS case No.98 dated 25-4-2007 under sections 143/447/427/506 of the Penal Code was started and after enquiry police submitted charge-sheet No. 355 on 6-9-2007 against the accused-petitioner and 3 others under sections 143/447/427/506 of the Penal Code for trespassing into their land filling sand thereof. 

 9. On perusal of the records, it appears that charge-sheet has filed against the accused-petitioner and three others under sections 143/447/ 427/506 of the Penal Code. Now let us see whether any of these sections are tenable against the accused-petitioner in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 10. The facts as disclosed in the FIR and charge-sheet do not disclose any offence under section 143 of the Penal Code because for committing an offence of unlawful assembly under section 143 of the Penal Code, there must be assembly of five or more persons as required under section 141 of the Penal Code, but the charge-sheet of the instant case discloses that only four persons i.e. the accused Nos. 1 to 4 including the petitioner have been placed for trial and, as such, there being less than five persons consisting of the alleged assembly there is no unlawful assembly within the meaning of section 143 of the Penal Code and hence the proceeding of the said case under section 143 of the Penal Code against the petitioner is liable to be quashed; that the facts as disclosed in the FIR and charge-sheet do not constitute any offence under section 427 of the Penal Code against the petitioner, because for constituting offence under section 427 of the Penal Code, there must be an mischief within the meaning of section 425 of the penal Code which requires the alleged action to cause loss or damage or destruction of any property or change in the property to diminish its value or utility or injury, but in the instant case admittedly the complainant cause earth filing for developing the land and the complainant alleged that the accused caused further earth filling, which rendered further development of the land and such development does not cause loss, damage destruction or change to the value or utility of the land in question as such the facts as disclosed does not constitute any mischief within the meaning of section 425 of the Penal Code and hence no offence under section 427 of the Penal Code has been constituted by petitioner and therefore the proceeding of this case under section 427 of the Penal Code is liable to be quashed. 

 14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the proceeding in GR Case No. 305 of 2007 arising out of Badda PS Case No. 98 dated 25-4-2007 under sections 143/447/427/506 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 15, Dhaka should be quashed so far as it relates to the accused-petitioner.
